title: Induction & Augmentation of Labor
keywords: no misoprostol with prior uterine surgery
sources: Critical Vector — OB Pocket Guide: Induction / Augmentation (ACOG 2023)
Grobman WA et al. NEJM 2018 (ARRIVE); ACOG Practice Bulletin on induction of labor

changelog.change: Initial entry — ripening/induction methods and dosing, oxytocin titration, tachysystole management, ARRIVE context.

summary: Choose the ripening method by the cervix (Bishop) and the uterine scar status: prostaglandins are contraindicated with a prior uterine incision — use a transcervical Foley balloon instead. Tachysystole is > 5 contractions per 10 minutes averaged over 30 minutes; stop or reduce the agent and resuscitate the fetus.

body.text: ARRIVE (2018): elective induction of a low-risk nullipara at 39 weeks did not raise the cesarean rate and may reduce perinatal morbidity — it is a reasonable option, not a mandate.

rows: Contraindicated with any prior uterine surgery. Do NOT run concurrently with oxytocin
Less tachysystole than the vaginal route; convenient
Removable if tachysystole; wait ≥ 30 min after removal before starting oxytocin
Purely mechanical; SAFE with a prior uterine scar; no tachysystole risk. Can combine with oxytocin or oral misoprostol
Usual max 20–40 mU/min; titrate to adequate contractions

items: Definition: > 5 contractions in 10 min, averaged over 30 min.
With a normal tracing: reduce or stop oxytocin; reposition; IV fluid bolus.
With a category-II/III tracing: stop oxytocin, left lateral, O2, IV bolus, and consider terbutaline 0.25 mg SC. Remove a dinoprostone insert.

body.text: A prior classical (vertical) uterine incision or ≥ 2 prior low-transverse cesareans is a contraindication to induction. For a single prior low-transverse cesarean attempting TOLAC, avoid all prostaglandins — a Foley balloon ± oxytocin only, with continuous monitoring.
